typeIdent.description:
Indicates explicit sub-type of entry.  Composed of the concatenation of the typeKey of the instance's type and all
of its base type's typeIdent

id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

allRoutes.description: All the declared {@link MlModel.Route routes} handled by the router.

project.description: The project for which this router is used. The router can only route to models that are part of that project.

relationType.description: The subtype of {@link MlSubjectToModelRelation} used to represent the relations between subjects and models.

title:
A {@link MlModel} routing mechanism based on timed relations between the individual {@link MlSubject} instances
and the {@link MlModel} instances.
The relations are represented with a subtype of {@link MlSubjectToModelRelation}.

This router is the default behavior in a {@link MlProject}.
It is designed to address the common use case where the subject is an asset on which a few models are deployed,
and for which many predictions are computed during its lifecycle.

**Performance considerations**: note that for each deployed model, an instance of the relation will be persisted
*for each* subject to which it applies. Also, each update of status (e.g. promoting a model to champion) will
create new instances. The overall space complexity of this representation in the relational data store is
*O(M·S·C)* where *M* is the number of models, *S* the number of subjects and *C* the number of status changes.
name: MlModel.RelationRouter
